How to read this

Source: U.S. Department of Education Campus Safety and Security data (Clery Act), survey years 2020–2024, as supplied. "Sexual offenses" sums rape, fondling, incest and statutory rape. Each institution's figures are summed across every campus it reports.

On campus includes residence halls; residence halls are shown as their own shade so they are not counted twice. Off campus combines noncampus property (buildings the school owns or controls away from campus, such as Greek houses and study-abroad sites) and public property immediately adjacent to campus. Incidents elsewhere in the surrounding city are not part of these files.

These are reports, not prevalence. A higher count can reflect a stronger reporting culture and better-staffed Title IX offices as much as more incidents, so compare with care. Private includes nonprofit and for-profit schools, from the IPEDS control field. In the per-student view, top-school lists only include institutions with at least 5,000 students so very small schools do not dominate on a handful of reports. A few single-year spikes reflect historical cases reported all at once, most visibly the University of Michigan in 2020 (2,142 on-campus reports, largely tied to the Robert Anderson case), so five-year totals and rates for those schools are dominated by that year. Enrollment is the Clery "institution size" figure; regions come from the IPEDS 2023 directory; the 2026 U.S. News top 50 is applied to every year.
